question.problem: In an online poker tournament, the maximum loss is $10$ dollars, and the maximum win is $8$ dollars. Assuming that a player's earnings are uniformly distributed between $-10$ and $8,$ what is the probability that a randomly chosen player loses between $2$ and $8$ dollars?
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the earnings of a randomly chosen player. From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U[-10,8],$ and we wish to compute $P(-8\le X\le -2).$

In general, if $X∼U[a,b],$ then $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a}, & a\le x\le b \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

So, for our random variable $X∼U[-10,8],$ we have the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}, & -10\le x\le 8 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-8\le X\le -2) & ={\int }_{-8}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-8}^{-2}\frac{1}{18}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{x}{18}|}_{-8}^{-2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{18}-(-\frac{8}{18}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
